commit_message:
avformat/mlvdec: demux LJ92 huffman comressed frames

A minimal DNG header is added to each LJ92 compressed frame, allowing
thme to be decoded by the TIFF decoder. The TIFF decoder is responsible
for setting up the MJPEG decoder, signalling the correct s->bayer flag,
and setting pix_fmt.

The LJ92 compressed frames can be muxed out to DNG files, and manipulated
in DNG software. Tested with darktable and rawtherapee.

Contributor: South East <8billion.people@gmail.com>

fix_commit_message:
avformat/mlvdec: fix size checks

Fixes: heap-buffer-overflow
Fixes: 391962476/clusterfuzz-testcase-minimized-ffmpeg_dem_MLV_fuzzer-5746746587676672

Found-by: continuous fuzzing process https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/tree/master/projects/ffmpeg
Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 251d43aef0df on top of intro 86dd15fd0dd0 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (IntegerOverflow): The MLV demuxer's LJ92 frame-decoding path (added to support demuxing LJ92 huffman-compressed frames) computes a packet payload `size` from attacker-controlled fields in the MLV bitstream (block size, timestamp/frame fields, optional crop/pan fields for video, and a variable-length `space` field) without sufficiently validating that the resulting value is non-negative/in-range. This unchecked `size` is then used both to allocate a packet buffer (`av_new_packet(pkt, size + MAX_HEADER_SIZE)`) and to read that many bytes into it (`avio_read(pbio, pkt->data + header_size, size)`), and separately to compute the audio packet length. A crafted MLV file can cause `size` to underflow (since `size` is an unsigned int subtracted by attacker-controlled `space`) or otherwise reach values that make `size + MAX_HEADER_SIZE` overflow, resulting in a heap buffer overflow when the actual read/allocate sizes disagree. Root cause: Missing/insufficient bounds validation on an attacker-controlled `size` (and the related `space` field) before it is used in unsigned arithmetic (subtraction that can underflow) and in a size-plus-constant allocation (addition that can overflow), both feeding directly into memory allocation and copy operations.
